title: Identify Evolving Technologies in the Cloud

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud platforms provide the massive compute capacity and managed services needed to support rapidly evolving technologies.
CompTIA focuses this objective on two major areas: machine learning and artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things.
You need to recognize the function being performed, not become an artificial intelligence scientist or Internet of Things engineer.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: What type of information is being understood, generated, sensed, converted, or transmitted?
sections.callout: Input + desired output → identify the technology.

sections.title: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI)
paragraphs: Machine learning and artificial intelligence services allow systems to analyze information, identify patterns, make classifications, convert information between formats, or generate new content.
For Cloud+, focus on recognizing the job each capability performs.

entries.title: Text Recognition
paragraphs: Text recognition identifies written or printed characters from an input.
An example would be extracting text from a scanned document or image.
Think: See writing → turn it into usable text.
entries.recognitionCue: If a system needs to identify text contained in an image or document → think text recognition.

entries.title: Text Translation
paragraphs: Text translation converts written information from one language into another.
Think: English text → Spanish text.
entries.recognitionCue: If written language must be converted to another language → think text translation.

entries.title: Visual Recognition
paragraphs: Visual recognition identifies or classifies information contained in images.
It can detect what an image contains.
Think: What am I looking at?
entries.recognitionCue: If the artificial intelligence service needs to recognize objects or content inside an image → think visual recognition.

entries.title: Sentiment Analysis
paragraphs: Sentiment analysis attempts to determine the attitude or emotional tone contained in text.
For example, an organization could analyze customer feedback to determine whether comments are positive, negative, or neutral.
Think: How does this person feel about it?
entries.recognitionCue: If the goal is identifying attitude or emotional tone from text → think sentiment analysis.

entries.title: Voice-to-Text
paragraphs: Voice-to-text converts spoken audio into written text.
Think: Hear it → write it.
entries.recognitionCue: If speech must become written words → think voice-to-text.

entries.title: Text-to-Voice
paragraphs: Text-to-voice converts written text into spoken audio.
Think: Read it → speak it.
entries.recognitionCue: If written information must be spoken aloud automatically → think text-to-voice.

entries.title: Generative AI
paragraphs: Generative artificial intelligence creates new content based on input and patterns learned from data.
Generated output can include text, images, code, and other digital content.
Think: Not just classify something—create something new.
entries.recognitionCue: If the system is generating new content from a prompt or input → think generative AI.

sections.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
paragraphs: The Internet of Things connects physical devices capable of collecting, communicating, or acting on information.
Cloud platforms can receive and process information from large numbers of Internet of Things devices.
Think: Physical world talks to the digital world.

entries.title: Sensors
paragraphs: A sensor measures something in the physical environment.
Examples include temperature, motion, pressure, and humidity.
Think: Sensor = collect information.
entries.recognitionCue: If the device measures conditions in the physical environment → think sensor.

entries.title: Gateways
paragraphs: An Internet of Things gateway acts as an intermediary between devices and other networks or cloud systems.
It can collect or forward device communications.
Think: Gateway = bridge between the devices and the wider network.
entries.recognitionCue: If many Internet of Things devices need an intermediary to reach cloud services → think gateway.

entries.title: Communication
paragraphs: Internet of Things devices must communicate so their collected information can reach other systems.
Communication describes the exchange of that information between devices, gateways, and cloud environments.
Think: The data must get from the thing to somewhere useful.
entries.recognitionCue: If the issue involves how Internet of Things devices exchange information → think communication.

entries.title: Transmission Protocols
paragraphs: Transmission protocols define the rules used to move Internet of Things information between systems.
Different environments may use different protocols depending on their communication requirements.
For this objective, the recognition target is the concept: a communication system needs agreed rules for transmitting information.
Think: Protocol = rules of the conversation.
entries.recognitionCue: If the scenario asks what defines how Internet of Things information is exchanged → think transmission protocol.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Extract writing from an image or document → Text recognition
Convert one written language to another → Text translation
Identify contents of an image → Visual recognition
Determine positive or negative attitude → Sentiment analysis
Speech becomes words → Voice-to-text
Words become speech → Text-to-voice
Create new content → Generative AI
Measure physical environment → Internet of Things sensor
Bridge devices to a network or cloud → Gateway
Devices exchange data → Communication
Rules governing data transmission → Transmission protocols

entries.title: Text Recognition vs. Visual Recognition
paragraphs: Both may involve images. Text recognition identifies written characters; visual recognition identifies what the image contains.
A picture of a dog points to visual recognition. A photo of a receipt whose words must be extracted points to text recognition.

entries.title: Voice-to-Text vs. Text-to-Voice
paragraphs: Follow the direction: spoken input to written output means voice-to-text; written input to spoken output means text-to-voice.

entries.title: Generative AI vs. Recognition
paragraphs: Recognition systems primarily identify or classify existing information. Generative artificial intelligence produces new content.

entries.title: Sensor vs. Gateway
paragraphs: A sensor gathers information. A gateway connects or forwards information.
The temperature device collecting the reading is the sensor. The intermediary forwarding readings toward the cloud is the gateway.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Image contains words that must be extracted → Text recognition
Written language must change languages → Text translation
Need to identify objects in an image → Visual recognition
Determine whether customer comments are positive or negative → Sentiment analysis
Speech must become written text → Voice-to-text
Written text must become spoken audio → Text-to-voice
System must create new content → Generative AI
Measure real-world condition → Internet of Things sensor
Connect devices toward the cloud → Gateway
Internet of Things systems exchange information → Communication
Rules determine how device data is transmitted → Transmission protocol
Detect what exists → Recognition
Create something new → Generative AI
